) } ``` The **product page** (`/workspace/app/product/page.tsx`) has no navigation elements -- it does not link back to the home page or anywhere else. It only displays product data. --- ## 4. Premium Widget

{inventory.count} in stock

Price: ${inventory.price}

) } ``` Key observations: - The component is an **async function** (`async function ProductPage`), making it a **React Server Component (RSC)** that can directly `await` data. - It imports `getInventory` from `@/lib/data` (which resolves to `/workspace/lib/data.ts`). ### Data Source: `getInventory()` **`/workspace/lib/data.ts`**: ```tsx import { connection } from 'next/server' export async function getInventory() { await connection() return { count: Math.floor(Math.random() * 50), price: (Math.random() * 100).toFixed(2), } } ``` Key observations: - It imports `connection()` from `next/server`, which is a **Next.js 16 experimental API** used to signal that the component depends on a dynamic/real-time data source. Calling `await connection()` tells Next.js to opt that page out of static generation and treat it as dynamic (SSR on each request). - The data is **randomized** on each call (random count 0-49, random price 0-99.99), confirming it is meant to be dynamic per-request data. ### Home Page: No Data Fetching The home page (`/workspace/app/page.tsx`) is a plain synchronous component with no data fetching at all. --- ## 5. Loading States and Suspense Boundaries **There are no loading states or Suspense boundaries anywhere in this codebase.** Specifically: - No `loading.tsx` files exist in any route segment. - No `` components are used. - No `error.tsx` or `not-found.tsx` files exist. This means the product page will **block the entire page render** while `getInventory()` resolves -- the browser will show nothing until the data is ready. In a production app, you would typically either: - Add a `loading.tsx` file at `/workspace/app/product/loading.tsx`, or - Wrap the data-dependent part in `` with a fallback. --- ## 6. How the Title is Rendered on the Product Page The product page title comes from **two sources**: 1. **Root Layout Metadata** (`/workspace/app/layout.tsx`): ```tsx export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'Shop', description: 'E-commerce product store', } ``` This sets the `` tag to "Shop" globally in the `<head>`. The product page does **not** export its own `metadata`, so it inherits the root layout's title ("Shop"). 2. **In-page `<h1>`** (`/workspace/app/product/page.tsx`): ```tsx <h1>Premium Widget</h1> ``` This is the visible heading on the page. It is **hardcoded** -- not derived from any data source. 3. **Sub-headings** show dynamic data from `getInventory()`: ``` <p>{inventory.count} in stock</p> <p>Price: ${inventory.price}</p> ``` --- ## Summary of All Relevant File Paths | File | Role | |---|---| | `/workspace/package.json` | Project config, dependency versions | | `/workspace/next.config.ts` | Next.js config with `cacheComponents: true` | | `/workspace/tsconfig.json` | TypeScript config with `@/*` path alias | | `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` | Root layout; sets global `<title>Shop` | | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | Home page (`/`); links to `/product` | | `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` | Product page (`/product`); async RSC, fetches inventory | | `/workspace/lib/data.ts` | Data module; `getInventory()` with `connection()` for dynamic SSR | session_id: ses_02d391c1fffe3rn8zo6wE3XiY8
